newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on technical buying.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher on Wednesday, as local investors actively bought on technical factors after prices plunged yesterday, traders said.
Prices ranged from 130 to 310 yen per tonne higher, with benchmark May 1998 closing 290 yen higher at 14,380 yen.
The day's estimated trade volume was 73,998 lots.
Active buying from individual investors supported the market throughout the day, traders said.
"Most investors assumed the fall on Tuesday was overdone," a commodities brokerage house trader said.
On Tuesday, Tokyo corn futures closed down by their daily 500-yen limit across-the-board.
At 0755 GMT, the spot May corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was at $2.87-1/4 per bushel, down from the $2.89-1/4 Tuesday close.
The spot May soybean contract on the CBOT overnight trading system stood at $8.79-1/4 per bushel, against the previous close of $8.80-1/4.
